I am a keen observer of US politicking and electioneering. I like to watch fireworks for the same basic reason, the absurdity of the expense and concussive force of the display is addictive. That being said I have some issues with the way the 2016 campaign is beginning.

I think no matter what you believe or wish for it's a forgone conclusion that if there are no dramatic developments between now and the election, Hillary Clinton will be the next POTUS.

I dislike the notion of dynasty as much as the next guy but the thing is she and Bill married because they are similar in ambition skill and political will. It's less of a dynasty and more of a partnership of two like minded people. I think a good and fair analogy is whenever a vice president succeeds a successful president. A real dynasty is hereditary and nepotistic. Like the situation in Canada at the moment where a well remembered Prime Minister's son is running for PM based mainly on name recognition and good hair, or in India where the Gandhi dynasty continues to shape political thought.

H. Clinton is a skilled and capable leader worthy of the office as are some of her opponents in this race. I try to avoid partisanship and I am frustrated because I find myself without a party which represents my views but this time around the right is almost a joke but will still get somewhere in the %40's on election day to the left's %50's and the polls at this point seem to favor and H. Clinton coronation for her to inherit of the will of the left. So I think it's not unreasonable to say that she will be the next POTUS.

So this isn't a dynasty, that's not my worry.

As such I am already fed up with the thinly veiled attacks from closet bigots on all sides about the gender issue. The most annoying thing is that most of this type of absurdity seems to be coming from the Clinton camp itself. if you ignore the type of people you'd ignore about the race issue in 2008 like the KKK and the neo-Nazi's and the Rush Limbaugh acolytes and the Trumps then the whole debate seems to me to focus on her skills and ability as a politician and leader rather than her gender.

When I see articles asking if she's ready or not I can almost without reading the article be assured that I'm about to read the writings of a closeted bigot. I'm sick of tolerating this nonsense.

It's not her gender. This goes almost without saying but needs to be said in order to preempt the type of accusations of prejudice that Clinton critics seem to be susceptible to. I'm not worried about gender.

There are enough questions there to merit serious debate without resorting to the outdated and boring gender argument. She won't be doing manual labor as president so how could there be a difference between her style of administration and anyone else's other than policy.

She has the experience and credentials and the history of scandals and successes that all career politicians have at her age.

I'd like it more if this election was more competitive or if money and campaign finance were not an issue. I'd love to see spirited debate in the primaries with Warren Sanders Biden Clinton and many more at the local state and federal level and the same thing on the republican primary trail. I'd like to have a meaningful and raucous convention cycle where the spirit of a party is divided and galvanized and spawns third and fourth parties on all sides with opposing and diverse opinions and excellent debate is had by all.

I'd like that but I know as well as the next person that it will take more than what H. Clinton can offer to get to this point. The parties are too entrenched in the USA for people to imagine what it was like before the party primary system seemed like a constitutional requirement for an election. That's what I find so frustrating about H. Clinton. She can whip her party with a slave driver's precision and it's not really because of her skill in leadership. It's because that's what the members of congress and senate and all tiers of government down to county sheriff expect.

She is inheriting the will of the party not because of dynastic or nepotistic corruption but because she put the time in, and the gears that are invisibly and inexorably governed by the human tendency to lose a republic to the much easier to manage oligarchy have allowed the lazy majority to put her there.

The tragedy is that she could have done it herself. She need not pander like she does. She need not spend literally billions from corporations on electioneering to oblige herself to their wills to accomplish trivial quarterly profit motives. This is how she has been taught the gears work just like nearly all of her recent predecessors but this is a terrible misapplication of real politic that will destroy the greatest republic the world has ever known.

What I am concerned about in this election is that entirely too much money from entirely too few people are the fueling the main engine of discourse in the USA. I am concerned that corruption is no longer a sideshow to the real workings of government and is now the principal motivating element. Lobbyist have their own lobby. The special interest have given up trying to run for office and would rather commandeer the will of those already in office.

This is the cancer that Clinton has dedicated her entire life to. Like the cell that just wants to operate normally but does so by imitating cells around it and just dividing and growing and replicating itself to "get the message out" as loudly and as widely as possible. She grew up in this environment and it has been becoming more and more malignant as she has become more and more powerful.

She comes by it honestly. The roman empire fell over the course of 400 years. It started to fall during the last stages of it's republic and became doomed with the accession of the Caesars. That it took a further 400 years to actually fail is a product of the early successes of the republican citizenry rather than the triumphs of the emperors of the late first century that marked the peak of Roman domination. This is human nature, a pattern that has repeated itself over and over since time immemorial and it is so easy to interrupt.

Don't elect Clinton.

She is morally bankrupt and she is oblivious to it. That's the only reason. It doesn't matter that she is left wing, liberal, wealthy, beholden to the corporations or a woman. Her political career is based on the worst excesses and flaws within the USA right now.

Don't elect anyone. Run for office yourself. Get someone you trust to hold your local interests in mind to run for office and start their campaign. Do something. DO IT. It's your responsibility as a citizen to just go out and fail in the name of your country. The world needs America but not the American empire. Please just stop imagining that you have only two options when the election comes. Stop imagining that there are only two real contests for nominations. Otherwise you are the cancer that will eat the USA out of power and destroy the relative peace that the world enjoys because of it's overwhelming power.

What is a leader? When do they actually exist and when are people we identify as leaders just figure heads who don't truly lead anything? An ecosystem doesn't have leaders, but should we call its apex predators the leader because the predators are the biggest or the microbiome because it directs all other life in the ecosystem (including the apex predators)?

Is true leadership of complex organisational structures a myth? Is the leadership narrative just another pattern bias our primitive minds use to feel safe that we inherited from our hunter gather tribal anscestors, but doesn't work for understanding modern social structures?

Do microbiomes have moral obligations? Do locust swarms have moral obligations? Does the fish in the front of a school of fish have moral obligations? Does the first goose in a V formation have moral obligations?

What make us and our organizational structures different or special above all other complex organizational structures in nature?

Whether they do or not probably depends on that leader and their sense of ethics.

Whether they should or not is a completely different question.
Yes, the real question is do they actually have morals.

Depends. IF they are a leader because of tradition, then no, because tradition is what got them there and what binds them, they only owe what the tradition demands of them. IF they are a leader because of a philosophy then it depends on if that philosophy demands moral obligations, if so then yes, if not then no. If they are a leader because of charisma and a cult of personality, then they only have the moral obligations they put upon themselves.
I think that's a good point. If part of their job is to represent the people, then I think it's fair to hold them morally responsible for representing the interests of the people.
